jobs.title: Global Security Manager
jobs.description:
We are an applied AI lab building end-to-end software agents.

We're the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer.

Our team is extremely talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro.

Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us.

Role Mission

Cognition is growing fast, with teams in San Francisco, New York, London, Berlin, Tokyo, Singapore, Sydney and other cities, and customers that include some of the largest and most security-conscious institutions in the world, including the U.S. government. As a frontier AI company, our people, our offices and the systems we build are attractive targets for nation-state actors, criminals and activists.

The Global Security Manager builds and runs the program that protects Cognition's people, facilities, travel and events worldwide, and the physical and personnel security that supports our Federal division. This is a hands-on, high-trust role: you will set strategy and policy, run day-to-day security operations through a small team and trusted vendors, and be the decision-maker when something goes wrong. You will report to the Chief Security Officer and work closely with Threat Intel & Investigations, Corporate Security, IT, Workplace, People, Legal and the Federal team.

What You'll Accomplish

Risk & Threat Assessment: Monitor geopolitical, environmental, physical and cyber threats globally. Run threat and vulnerability assessments for offices, offsites, events and executive travel destinations, and partner with Threat Intel & Investigations on threats directed at our employees and leadership.
Policy & Strategy Development: Create and enforce security policies, standard operating procedures, emergency response plans and compliance standards worldwide, with a physical security strategy that scales as we open new offices and markets.
Crisis Management & Incident Response: Lead responses to safety threats, travel emergencies and critical incidents, from workplace violence to natural disasters. Own incident command, the mass notification system, and business continuity planning with Legal, People, Workplace and IT, and run post-incident reviews that turn every event into lasting improvements.
Physical Security Operations & Technology: Own access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection and visitor management across our offices. Set security standards for new office build-outs, and integrate physical access with our identity systems alongside Corporate Security and IT.
Team & Vendor Oversight: Manage security personnel, the security operations center (GSOC), and external guard, executive protection and technology vendors. Set performance metrics, manage contracts and budget, and hold partners to a high bar.
Travel & Executive Protection: Oversee global travel risk programs, tracking tools, pre-trip briefings and high-risk journey management. Run the executive protection program for our CEO and leadership team, including advance work, residential security assessments and event security.
Counterintelligence: Build Cognition's counterintelligence program to identify and counter efforts by foreign intelligence services and competitors to gain access to our people, technology and customers, including targeted recruitment, social engineering and elicitation. Provide regular counterintelligence briefings to executives and staff, especially before foreign travel, and partner with Threat Intelligence, the Facility Security Officer and government counterparts on suspected incidents.
Federal Division Security: Interface with our Facility Security Officer, who owns cleared facilities and personnel security, to provide appropriate protections in support of our FedRAMP, ITAR and IL5+ operations, including physical access controls, visitor and foreign-national controls, and insider risk programs.
External Partnerships: Build relationships with local and federal law enforcement, OSAC and peer security teams at other AI labs and technology companies to stay ahead of emerging risks and coordinate during incidents.
Automate with Devin: Use Devin and other AI agents to scale the program: threat and travel monitoring, alert triage, reporting and the operational work that usually requires a large headcount.

Exceptional Candidates Have Demonstrated

Program leadership: 8+ years in corporate or global security, including physical security, executive protection, GSOC operations and travel risk management, ideally at a fast-growing technology company. A background in law enforcement, the military or government is a plus.
Crisis judgment: Experience acting as the senior decision-maker during real incidents, staying calm under pressure, and communicating clearly to executives and employees.
Global, distributed operations: A track record of building or scaling security programs across multiple countries, including selecting and managing third-party vendors and owning a budget.
Industrial security: Familiarity with NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117) and ITAR, and experience working alongside Facility Security Officers to support cleared programs.
Discretion and writing: Strong written communication and the judgment to operate in a confidential, high-trust environment.
Builder mindset: Comfort working in a dynamic environment, moving quickly, and replacing manual processes with tooling and automation.
Background: Prior law enforcement, military, or intelligence experience is required.
Eligibility: US Citizen required, must be clearable to TS/SCI. Previous or current clearance is a plus. Ability to travel and to be available outside business hours during incidents. Certifications such as CPP or PSP are a plus.

Job Description

We are looking for an experienced, results-driven Transformation Manager / Technical Program Manager to lead complex global transformation programs. The main focus is coordinating the decommissioning of legacy systems in an international IT environment.

The ideal candidate is an expert in end-to-end program management. They can turn IT objectives into clear technology roadmaps that teams can deliver, covering legacy system retirement, enterprise system integration and the move to target platforms. They work closely with architects, developers, application owners and infrastructure teams.

The role calls for strong cross-functional leadership, strategic stakeholder management, and a solid background in Agile and Kanban delivery. It also requires experience leading globally distributed teams and giving executive-level governance and reporting.

Responsibilities:

Transformation & Technology Roadmap Ownership

Turn IT objectives and target architecture goals into clear, prioritized technology roadmaps and delivery plans.
Lead complex, global transformation programs from start to finish, from initiation and planning through execution, transition and closure.
Define program scope, milestones, dependencies and success metrics, and keep them aligned with IT strategy and business needs.
Manage program risks, issues and dependencies across several workstreams and handle them proactively.
Drive change management so new platforms and ways of working are adopted successfully.

Enterprise System Integration & Technical Delivery

Plan and coordinate enterprise system integration across several platforms, applications and regions.
Work closely with architects and developers to make sure solutions are technically sound, scalable and in line with the target architecture.
Turn IT requirements into technical deliverables, and make sure technical constraints are understood at management level.
Oversee release planning, cutover activities and handovers to operations.

Legacy System Decommissioning

Coordinate the full decommissioning of legacy applications, systems and infrastructure, from start to finish.
Build and maintain the inventory of legacy systems, including dependency mapping, interfaces, data flows and contracts.
Define the order and waves of decommissioning, and align them with migration timelines and business continuity needs.
Coordinate data migration, archiving and retention with application owners, data owners and Compliance.
Make sure security, regulatory and audit requirements are met before systems are switched off.
Manage the controlled shutdown of systems, licenses, infrastructure and support contracts, and track the cost savings realized.
Keep decommissioning status, risks and progress visible through Jira, ServiceNow and ADO.

Agile Delivery & Ways of Working

Run delivery using Agile and Kanban methods, including backlog management, flow optimization and continuous improvement.
Set up and maintain Jira dashboards, boards and roadmaps to give clear visibility of progress, capacity and blockers.
Run Agile ceremonies and Kanban practices, such as WIP limits and flow metrics, across distributed teams.
Encourage a results-driven, collaborative and transparent delivery culture.

Stakeholder Management & Executive Governance

Build strong relationships with senior and executive stakeholders across IT, business, application owners and vendors.
Set up and run program governance structures, including steering committees, decision logs and escalation paths.
Prepare clear, concise executive-level status reports, dashboards and presentations, including decommissioning progress and cost savings.
Manage expectations, negotiate priorities and help stakeholders reach decisions when their interests conflict.

Global Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Coordination

Lead and motivate globally distributed, cross-functional teams across different time zones and cultures.
Coordinate work between internal teams, infrastructure teams, external partners and service providers.
Make sure roles, responsibilities and accountabilities are clear across the program.
Mentor team members and promote best practices in program and delivery management.

5-7 years of experience in program management, technical program management or transformation management in an international IT environment.
Proven experience coordinating legacy system decommissioning, including dependency analysis, data migration and archiving, and switching systems off.
Proven ability to turn IT objectives into technology roadmaps that teams can deliver.

Strong expertise in Agile delivery; hands-on Kanban experience is a strong plus.
Experience working closely with architects and developers on technical solution delivery.

This is not a routine processing role. You are expected to analyse customer profiles and transaction patterns comprehensively, apply risk-based judgment, and document your findings in clear, structured reports. You will work closely with the AML/CTF Compliance Officer, escalating matters with clear evidence and supporting final risk decisions.

What You Will Work On

Customer Due Diligence (CDD/OCDD/ECDD): Operate the end to end customer due diligence lifecycle, from onboarding CDD (Customer Due Diligence) through trigger-based ECDD (Enhanced Customer Due Diligence) and Ongoing Customer Due Diligence (OCDD). Handle Identity Verification (IDV), review and reassess Customer Risk Assessment (CRA) outputs, and perform additional identity checks as required.
Transaction Monitoring: Review transaction monitoring alerts to identify structuring, unusual fund movements, and unexpected transaction patterns. Use the available monitoring channels to conduct investigations and escalations, and document the outcomes in clear reports.
Sanctions and Screening: Investigate alerts against global sanctions and PEP lists. Accurately discount false positives, and escalate true matches or higher risk profiles with clear evidence. Conduct adverse media searches where relevant.
Suspicious Matter Reporting (SMR) Support: Own internal investigations and draft clear, structured investigation memos and SMR drafts so that the AML/CTF Compliance Officer can make a final determination. Prepare the supporting evidence needed for AUSTRAC reporting, and maintain SMR registers and case files.
Quality Assurance (QA) and Operational Management: Conduct QA reviews and maintain AML operational metrics. Support management reporting and internal and external audit and review activities.
AML Systems Operations and Cross-Functional Support: Operate the in-house AML systems proficiently, and translate operational pain points and improvement needs into structured feedback and requirements for the engineering and product teams. In addition, provide clear responses and guidance on AML-related enquiries escalated from customer-facing channels (e.g., Customer Support) to enable consistent handling across the organisation.

What We Are Looking For

Must-Have

5 + years of hands-on experience in AML/CTF operations (preferably within fintech, remittance service provider, e-money, payment institution, or banking environments)
End-to-End operational experience across customer due diligence (CDD/OCDD/ECDD), sanctions and PEP screening, risk assessment, and transaction monitoring
Analytical and critical thinking skills: able to go beyond checklist reviews, connect the dots in complex financial data, and make sound, independent risk-based judgments
Investigation and reporting: experience conducting internal investigations and drafting detailed escalation reports to support SMR filings
System proficiency: strong ability to use and adapt quickly to automated AML monitoring, screening, and case management tools
Communication: ability to articulate risks and investigation findings clearly in both written and verbal communication

Preferred

Familiarity with the Australian AML/CTF regulatory environment and AUSTRAC supervisory practices
Experience monitoring remittance or payment products
Experience working in a multicultural environment and collaborating with a global headquarters

What We Offer

Take ownership of the day to day operations of the Toss AU AML/CTF programme, which is already live, contributing to executing and continuously enhancing a stabilised framework
Work closely with the Toss AU AML/CTF Compliance Officer, owning the quality and consistency of Toss AU's AML operations
Where relevant, collaborate with the Korea headquarters AML team and other global functions to contribute to systems improvement and alignment with global standards
Competitive compensation package
Flexible and supportive work environment

Hiring Process

2 functional interviews (AML expertise, regulatory handling, execution capability)
2 culture fit interviews (e.g., way of working)

Pre-employment checks, including a National Police Check and Bankruptcy Check, will be conducted as part of the hiring process.

jobs.description:
The Chevron Engineering and Innovation Excellence Center (ENGINE) in Bengaluru India brings together the resources and expertise of the Chevron global network with talent in India to enhance agility and technological innovation to optimize solutions for the world’s current and future energy challenges. As one of the leading energy providers worldwide, Chevron is involved in the production of crude oil and natural gas, manufacturing of transportation fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals, and additives, and the development of enabling technologies.

Chevron's vision is to be the global energy company most admired for its people, partnerships, and performance. With a clear purpose to develop affordable, reliable, ever-cleaner energy that enables human progress, we believe human ingenuity has the power to solve any challenge and overcome any obstacle. Meeting the world’s growing energy needs requires the pursuit of innovations and advancements that deliver a better future for all.

About The Position

Transform enterprise data into clear business insights, trusted metrics, and decision-ready reporting for Chevron stakeholders. The Data Analyst partners with business teams, Product Owners, data engineers, and subject-matter experts to define analytical requirements, validate data, build dashboards, investigate trends, and communicate actionable recommendations

Key Responsibilities

Business and analytical requirements

Partner with business stakeholders to understand objectives, processes, decisions, pain points, and key performance indicators.
Translate business questions into analytical requirements, metric definitions, data needs, acceptance criteria, and reporting specifications.
Facilitate discovery sessions and document assumptions, calculation logic, dimensions, filters, thresholds, and data ownership.
Maintain a business glossary and ensure consistent use of approved metric definitions across reports and dashboards.

Data analysis and insight generation

Use SQL, Excel, Power BI, Python, or approved analytical tools to profile, combine, validate, and analyze structured and semi-structured data.
Perform descriptive, diagnostic, trend, variance, segmentation, correlation, and root-cause analysis.
Identify patterns, risks, anomalies, operational gaps, and improvement opportunities; quantify business impact where supported by evidence.
Validate analytical results with subject-matter experts and clearly distinguish facts, assumptions, estimates, and recommendations.
Prepare concise insight summaries and decision support for operational teams, Product Owners, managers, and senior leaders.

Reporting and visualization

Design and maintain Power BI semantic models, dashboards, reports, KPI scorecards, and self-service analytical products.
Apply effective visualization, accessibility, drill-through, filtering, row-level security, and mobile-layout practices.
Develop DAX measures, Power Query transformations, calculated columns, and optimized data models.
Monitor report usage, performance, refresh reliability, and stakeholder adoption; automate recurring reporting where practical.

Data quality, governance, and collaboration

Perform data reconciliation and quality checks for completeness, validity, consistency, timeliness, duplicates, and outliers.
Work with data engineers and source-system owners to resolve defects and improve upstream data controls.
Follow Chevron requirements for cybersecurity, privacy, access control, confidential data, retention, and responsible use of analytics.
Document datasets, source-to-report logic, refresh schedules, ownership, known limitations, and support procedures.
Create backlog items in Azure DevOps, support Agile ceremonies, assist with UAT, and validate production releases.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Engineering, Computer Science, Business, or a related field.
5-10 years of experience in data analysis, business intelligence, reporting, operations analysis, or a comparable role.
Strong SQL skills and experience with relational databases, data warehouses, or lakehouse platforms.
Hands-on Power BI experience including Power Query, DAX, data modeling, visual design, refresh, and row-level security.
Advanced Excel skills and ability to perform profiling, reconciliation, trend, variance, and root-cause analysis.
Experience translating business requirements into metrics, dashboards, analytical outputs, and acceptance criteria.
Strong written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, and stakeholder-management skills. Preferred qualifications
Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300) or relevant Microsoft Fabric certification.
Experience with Python or R for manipulation, automation, statistics, or visualization.
Experience with Azure SQL, Azure Synapse Analytics, Azure Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, or data lake environments.
Knowledge of forecasting, experimentation, process control, or anomaly detection.
Experience analyzing energy, refinery, commercial, customer, asset, emissions, supply-chain, or operational data.
Experience with Microsoft Purview, data catalogs, Agile/Scrum, SAFe, and Azure DevOps.

Success measures

Accurate and timely dashboards with clearly defined, traceable, and accepted metrics.
Reduced manual reporting effort and improved report refresh reliability.
Faster identification of performance gaps, operational risks, and improvement opportunities.
Higher stakeholder adoption and confidence in analytical products.
Documented insights that lead to measurable business decisions or process improvements.

Chevron ENGINE supports global operations, supporting business requirements across the world. Accordingly, the work hours for employees will be aligned to support business requirements. The standard work week will be Monday to Friday. Working hours are 8:00am to 5:00pm or 1.30pm to 10.30pm.

What We Can Offer You

Everything we do at Chevron is guided by our values and our commitment to The Chevron Way.

Have the opportunity to take part in world-leading energy projects, advance your professional development and expand your career within an inclusive and collaborative workplace.

Join a workplace where innovation, collaboration and safety are at the core of how we work.
Work in thoughtfully designed environments that support focus, well-being, and innovation enhanced by digital tools that enable seamless collaboration.
Grow through structured learning, mentorship, and opportunities to contribute to impactful projects that align with Chevron’s values and business priorities.
Access comprehensive benefits that support your health, well-being, and work-life balance.
Engage with emerging technologies and digital solutions that are shaping the future of energy and enterprise.

How To Apply

To be a part of our success, click APPLY
to submit your application.

Chevron regrets that it is unable to sponsor employment Visas or consider individuals on time-limited Visa status for this position.

Privacy and Terms and Conditions

We respect the privacy of candidates for employment. This Privacy Notice sets forth how we will use the information we obtain when you apply for a position through this career site. If you do not consent to the terms of this Privacy Notice, please do not submit information to us.

Please access the Global Application Statements, select the country where you are applying for employment. By applying, you acknowledge that you have read and agree to the country specific statement.

jobs.description:
Are you ready to shape the future of risk assessment in the commercial insurance space? Join our dynamic team where your analytical expertise will directly impact global business decisions and portfolio performance!

About The Role

This role offers the opportunity to develop product expertise and analytical skills crucial to enhancing the profitability of global Property underwriting portfolio.

As a key team member, you will combine strong analytical capabilities, data-driven techniques and actuarial methodologies to analyze portfolios, enhance costing models and influence business decisions. You will work extensively with policy and costing data on Swiss Re's Stargate platform, taking ownership of key data products and developing analytical solutions to support portfolio impact assessments, reinsurance purchasing and underwriting decisions. Your work will directly contribute to portfolio steering, operational efficiency and the overall Business Unit's performance.

Key Responsibilities

Data Management & Analytical Development

Develop a comprehensive understanding of Property data flows across systems, from source to consumption.
Own and manage analytical data pipelines and transformations on Swiss Re’s Foundry-based data platform (Stargate). Collaborate with data engineering and technology teams to enhance data pipelines by defining business requirements and address data quality issues.
Design, build, test, and maintain business-focused analytical tools on the data platform. Translate underwriting and actuarial requirements into robust data products, analytical workflows, and user-friendly outputs, while supporting adoption and continuous improvement
Translate complex data into meaningful insights and communicate findings to Underwriters, Portfolio Managers and other stakeholders

Pricing & Portfolio Management

Support actuarial pricing and portfolio profitability assessments using experience rating, exposure rating and other quantitative techniques.
Contribute to pricing model enhancements, actuarial rate reviews and the evaluation of costing parameters.
Independently conduct case pricing using actuarial methodologies and effectively communicate findings with Underwriters and key stakeholders
Deliver technical insights that support financial performance management and portfolio steering across sub-portfolios

About The Team

We are a global team of actuarial and analytical professionals spread across Bangalore, Munich, Zurich, Manchester, London, New York, Windsor and Kansas City.

Our work combines actuarial expertise, data analytics and analytical development to improve pricing capabilities, generate portfolio insights and support data-driven business decisions. We collaborate closely with Underwriters, Portfolio Managers, Data Engineers and technology teams to develop practical solutions to complex business challenges. We play a critical role in supporting pricing decisions and steering one of the largest portfolios within the business.

We foster an inclusive culture that values diverse perspectives, collaboration and innovative thinking, offering opportunities to develop both technical and business expertise.

About You

You're an analytical problem-solver who thrives in a collaborative environment and enjoys translating complex data into actionable business insights. Your communication skills allow you to effectively partner with stakeholders across multiple functions and geographies.

We Are Looking For Candidates Who Meet These Requirements

Bachelor's/Master's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Actuarial Science, Data Science, Engineering, Economics or an equivalent quantitative field.
Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in actuarial, data analytics, quantitative modelling or related analytical roles, preferably within insurance or financial services
Strong proficiency in Python, SQL or R, with hands-on experience in data manipulation, analysis and automation
Experience working with large datasets, developing analytical solutions and ensuring data quality and accuracy
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to independently translate business requirements into practical analytical solutions.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present technical findings clearly to business stakeholders.
A proactive, solution-oriented mindset, with strong ownership, attention to detail and the ability to collaborate across global teams.
Experience with commercial property insurance products
Progress toward recognized actuarial qualifications will be a plus

Why Join Us?

Work in a multicultural, high-performing environment with global exposure
Influence high-impact portfolio decisions that shape business strategy
Collaborate with world-class experts across various business functions
Excellent opportunities for professional development and model innovation

Our company has a hybrid work model where the expectation is that you will be in the office at least three days per week

About Swiss Re

Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. We cover both Property & Casualty and Life & Health. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients. This is possible thanks to the collaboration of more than 15,000 employees across the world.

Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. We embrace a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.

Bedrijfsomschrijving

Bij Syngenta Crop Protection ontwikkelen we baanbrekende oplossingen die de wereldwijde voedselzekerheid beschermen en duurzame landbouw bevorderen. Als wereldmarktleider met ons hoofdkantoor in Zwitserland ondersteunen we telers met innovatieve gewasbeschermingstechnologieën die bestand zijn tegen de grootste uitdagingen van de natuur.

We combineren geavanceerde wetenschap met digitale oplossingen om slimme gewasbescherming te ontwikkelen die opbrengsten maximaliseert en tegelijk de impact op het milieu minimaliseert.

Sluit je aan bij onze missie om gewasbescherming van zaad tot oogst te vernieuwen.

Vacatureomschrijving

Technical Trial Data Analyst

Business Unit: Crop Protection B/NL
Afdeling: Technical Support
Locatie: Hybride en kantoor Bergen op Zoom

Als Technical Trial Data Analist vertaal je hoogwaardige data uit veldproeven naar heldere technische inzichten en overtuigende commerciële verhalen. Je helpt bij het plannen, uitvoeren en rapporteren van kleinschalige proeven en grootschalige split-fieldproeven bij telers. Daarmee versterk je technische introductieplannen, productdemonstraties en campagneondersteuning in België en Nederland.

Dit is een praktische, veldgerichte functie op het snijvlak van Technical Support, Sales, Marketing en Europese specialisten. Je combineert een solide proefopzet, data-analyse en visualisatie — waaronder data uit drones — met een goed begrip van de behoeften van telers en commerciële prioriteiten.

Wat ga je doen?

Een afgesproken portfolio van veldproeven voor gewasbescherming plannen, opzetten en uitvoeren: van de eerste voorbereiding tot dataverzameling (via Drones en gerichte bemonstering), analyse en eindrapportage, met een hoge mate van zelfstandigheid.
Datasets van meerdere proeven op commerciële bedrijven beheren, inclusief proefveldopzet, contact met telers en afstemming over vergoedingen.
Uitstekende proefkwaliteit waarborgen via robuust proefontwerp, kwaliteitsstandaarden en objectieve dataverzameling binnen herhaalde proeven en demonstratieproeven.
Proefdata verwerken en beheren in Syngenta-systemen, zodat betrouwbare data en interpretatie snel beschikbaar zijn.
Veld- en dronedata analyseren, kansen en knelpunten signaleren en heldere aanbevelingen doen voor projecten, introducties en campagnes.
Complexe datasets vertalen naar overtuigende presentaties, visualisaties en technische verhalen die Sales- en Marketingteams ondersteunen.
Effectieve demonstratielocaties ontwikkelen en uitvoeren, en bijdragen aan telersbijeenkomsten en activiteiten die klanten beïnvloeden.
Vertrouwde relaties opbouwen met lokale salesregio’s, Crop Advisors en Europese technische specialisten, en gedurende campagnecycli proactieve ondersteuning bieden.

Functie-eisen

Wat breng je mee?

Een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding in Agronomie, Milieukunde, Landbouw of een verwante richting.

jobs.title: Benefits Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.
Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.
Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.
Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.
Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The People Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

Build the people function from scratch, fast enough to keep up with 10x growth. You'll build the systems, programs, and team from nothing, and make them work before we outgrow them.
Reinvent people operations around AI. Doing this by hand doesn't scale to a workforce growing this fast on a team this lean. You'll put AI at the core of how the function runs, so a small team supports many times its number.
Shape the culture and comms as the company scales. When a company scales this quickly, staying connected and aligned doesn't happen on its own. You'll help shape internal comms, events, and rhythm that keep a multi-site team that's growing fast bound to a shared culture.

Role Scope

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager - Water
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Ulteig is seeking a Senior Project Manager - Water to provide independent direction and leadership for large, complex water resources, stormwater, and watershed projects and programs. This role owns project strategy and delivery, integrates technical and commercial considerations, and leads multidisciplinary teams through scope definition, planning, execution, risk resolution, and client decision-making. The position applies strong water-sector knowledge to align project approaches with client needs, regulatory requirements, portfolio priorities, and Ulteig's quality and financial expectations.

What You’ll Do

Provide independent project management direction for large, complex, high-profile, or multi-phase water resources, stormwater, and watershed projects and programs from pursuit and contracting through closeout.
Own project direction, planning, and execution, including scope, schedule, budget, resource strategy, quality, risk, change, communications, and delivery commitments.
Lead multidisciplinary teams of engineers, planners, scientists, technical specialists, project controls professionals, subconsultants, and external partners; clarify roles, establish accountability, and remove delivery obstacles.
Facilitate and negotiate project approaches, sequencing, staffing, deliverables, and solutions where technical requirements, client priorities, regulatory expectations, or resource constraints compete.
Lead proposal and contract development for complex assignments, including scope definition, work plans, fee development, assumptions, exclusions, commercial terms, and delivery strategy.
Manage project financial performance by monitoring forecasts, labor and subconsultant costs, contingency, and invoicing; take timely corrective action when performance varies from plan.
Proactively identify and resolve complex project risks, interdependencies, scope gaps, change requests, and contractual issues; escalate matters with significant client, financial, safety, quality, or reputational impact.
Serve as a senior point of contact for clients, agencies, and key stakeholders; communicate project status and trade-offs, guide decisions, manage expectations, and build consensus around practical paths forward.
Partner with technical leads to evaluate the assumptions, methods, limitations, and findings of hydrologic and hydraulic analyses, planning studies, regulatory strategies, design concepts, and deliverables, including evaluations of existing and future stormwater conditions. Confirm that technical memoranda, planning reports, specifications, standards, exhibits, and regulatory documentation receive appropriate technical review and support the approved scope, decision points, quality plan, and client objectives.
Coordinate projects involving stormwater planning, drainage and flood-risk analysis, watershed studies, MS4 and NPDES compliance, feasibility and alternatives evaluation, resilience, green infrastructure, and related water initiatives.
Align project goals and delivery strategies with broader programs, portfolios, market conditions, and business priorities; support program managers or business leaders with portfolio planning and resource decisions.
Improve project management practices by applying lessons learned, strengthening controls and governance, and mentoring project managers and project professionals. Partner with technical leaders to improve technical approaches, specifications, standards, quality-control practices, and deliverables, including consistent documentation of assumptions and lessons learned.

What We Expect From You

Bachelor's degree in engineering, project management, construction management, environmental science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Demonstrated success independently managing large, complex, or high-risk professional services projects or programs with responsibility for overall delivery and financial performance.
Demonstrated depth in one or more relevant areas of water resources, stormwater, watershed planning, hydrology and hydraulics, drainage, or related infrastructure and environmental services, supported by strong working knowledge across the services needed to guide project strategy and facilitate technical decisions. Ability to interpret hydrologic, hydraulic, and water-quality model outputs and GIS and CAD deliverables, recognize material assumptions and limitations, and explain their implications for project recommendations.
Demonstrated knowledge of stormwater best management practices (BMPs), green stormwater infrastructure (GSI), and nature-based solutions (NBS), including typical project types such as green streets and regional facilities, treatment mechanisms, and considerations affecting feasibility and implementation.
Advanced understanding of project management practices, including scope, schedule, budget, resource planning, risk, change control, quality, procurement, contracts, and stakeholder communications.
Experience developing and negotiating proposals, scopes, fees, schedules, contract terms, amendments, and change requests for complex client engagements.
Ability to interpret project financial information, identify performance trends, and make decisions that support client outcomes, delivery commitments, and sustainable project performance.
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed teams, influence without direct authority, resolve conflict, and gain commitment from technical, operational, and client stakeholders.
Ability to communicate complex technical, financial, and regulatory information clearly to clients, team members, senior leaders, agencies, and community stakeholders.
Sound judgment in balancing technical quality, public and environmental considerations, regulatory obligations, schedule, cost, risk, and client value.
Ability to coach and mentor other project professionals and contribute to consistent project management practices across the Water team.
Demonstrates openness to innovation by embracing and applying evolving technology and AI tools to enhance workflows, solve problems, and drive continuous improvement.
Must have authorization to work permanently in the U.S.

Additional Preferred Qualifications

Professional Engineer (PE) or Project Management Professional (PMP), or another credential relevant to the role's project and technical responsibilities.
Experience delivering municipal, utility, transportation drainage, watershed, flood-risk, or environmental water programs under a range of contracting models.
Experience with MS4 programs, NPDES requirements, TMDL implementation, pollutant-load reduction planning, green infrastructure, resilience, or nature-based solutions.
Familiarity with water resources tools such as EPA SWMM, InfoWorks ICM, HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, HydroCAD, SWAT, GIS, and CAD.

jobs.title: Policy Program Manager, Safeguards Regulatory
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As a Program Manager on Anthropic's Safeguards team, you'll help make sure we meet our obligations under AI safety laws and regulations around the world. Working closely with Legal, you'll turn new and emerging requirements into programs, controls, and deliverables. This requires a detailed understanding of how our models and products are built, evaluated and safeguarded. Your work will support Anthropic's commitment to developing AI safely and beneficially as the regulatory landscape evolves.

The responsibilities listed below are some examples of areas that someone in this role could own, depending on their experience and the team's needs.

Key Responsibilities

Manage and drive complex safety initiatives that identify, assess and mitigate risks from frontier models, from initial risk assessment through to the deployment of safeguards
Partner with the Safeguards incident management team to strengthen incident response and reporting processes, including the policies that determine how incidents are escalated and when they must be reported externally
Conduct post-incident reviews, and work with the subject matter experts for each harm area to incorporate the findings into model and product safeguards
Own the safety strategy and deliverables for AI systems used in high-risk settings, including risk assessments, technical documentation, and the information that deploying customers need to use those systems safely
Define the safety and risk controls that our models and products require, ensure that each control has an owner and a documented procedure, and confirm that it operates as intended
Partner closely with the owners of each risk area to develop a deep understanding of AI risks, safety evaluations and mitigation strategies, and use that understanding to prepare safety documentation, transparency reports and regulatory submissions

Minimum Qualifications

Experience in trust and safety, AI safety or a related field, including designing and implementing safeguards against misuse or harm
Understanding of AI safety, including the principal risk areas and the evaluations and safeguards used to address them, well enough to engage substantively with the technical experts responsible for them
Experience running risk assessment or harm mitigation programs from identification through to resolution
Experience translating policy or regulatory requirements into practical operational processes
Ability to drive complex, cross-functional programs to completion in a fast-moving environment, including with technical teams outside your own discipline
Clear written communication, including documentation for technical, legal and external audiences
Strong attention to detail, and the judgment to recognize when work is at risk and raise it early
Commitment to the safe development and deployment of AI

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI-specific regulation, such as the EU AI Act
Experience leading incident response programs, including escalation paths and external reporting obligations
Experience preparing safety documentation, transparency reports or regulatory submissions
Experience working with technical and research teams on safety evaluations

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$245,000—$285,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California:
We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Overview

Senior Global Project Manager

Be Part of One Team, One Purpose.

At Emmes Group
, we’re shaping the future of clinical research— where human intelligence meets cutting-edge technology
to drive meaningful advancements in healthcare. With over 47 years of scientific excellence
, we’ve led groundbreaking research in cell and gene therapy, vaccines, infectious diseases, ophthalmology, rare diseases, and neuroscience.

Through our two business units— Emmes, a full-service CRO
, and Veridix AI, our technology, data, and analytical solutions
—we are modernizing clinical trials and accelerating the development of life-changing therapies.

We believe that every clinical breakthrough starts with people
—people who are passionate, purpose-driven, and ready to make an impact.
At Emmes Group, we bring People, Science, and Technology together to collaborate with our customers and deliver global health impact.
Our culture is built on integrity, collaboration, and innovation
, ensuring that every challenge is met with perseverance and accountability.

The Sr. Global Project Manager (SGPM) is critical to the successful conduct of Biopharmaceutical-sponsored clinical trials as a matrix leader of the core project team. The SGPM is responsible for the successful delivery of a Biopharmaceutical project(s). The SGPM will be client-facing and serve as the internal lead of the project through the life cycle of the study, ensuring effective project delivery in agreement with contracted project timeline and budget. The SGPM directs project delivery by driving team and financial efficiency, work product quality, and is responsible for client satisfaction through strong relationship management.

Responsibilities

May serve as a primary lead for major project bids and multi trial initiatives.
Ensures that deliverables for assigned project(s) are completed according to the contract budget, schedule, and quality standards. Effectively manages projects in all areas of performance.
Develops strong working relationships with clients, executive management, and project staff.
Collaborates with stakeholders to manage project issues, proactively identify and mitigate risks and drive milestone achievement.
Serves as the primary point of contact for biopharma clients and demonstrates proficiency in knowledge and understanding of client needs.
Proactively prepares/presents study metrics to maintain transparency for internal/external stakeholders.
Tracks project deliverables against contract using Emmes' tools.
Leads execution of contract amendments/change orders by collaborating with Business Development, Contracts Department, and executive management.
Monitors trends and drives changes to the plan as needed; identifies risks to delivery and drives development of mitigation plans with the project team to be presented to the client.
Ensures adherence to quality control expectations and milestone timelines for delivery of contractually required reports and deliverables.
Prospectively manages client expectations.
Effectively manages project resources (i.e., budget, personnel, and subcontracts).
Supports the culture of the business unit according to Emmes core values.
Identifies and manages change to scope and requests for out of scope activities.
Presents in bid defense meetings in collaboration with Business Development
Leads development study management plans with core project team members.
Identifies and documents lessons learned from study successes and challenges to promote development of best practices.
Models and propagates Emmes' commitment to a culture of quality in all aspects of our deliverables, utilizing a solution based, science driven, value added approach in collaborating with clients.
Supports corporate and departmental initiatives upon request.
Fosters a global perspective amongst the project teams from a depth of understanding of the interdependences of project, teams and timelines.
Delegates tasks according to individual/team strengths on supported global projects.
May supervise GPM team members
Provides leadership for junior GPM staff through mentoring, guiding, and coaching.
Supports recruitment/retention strategies and related initiatives.
Assesses direct report training needs.
Approves timesheets, expense reports, and leave requests.
Collaboratively conducts performance and compensation review activities for direct reports.
Responsible for addressing employee relations issues and resolving problems.
Performs other duties as assigned
Complies with all policies and standards

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree Scientific discipline. Required
12+ Years demonstrating scientific principles appropriate in managing a clinical research portfolio, including multi-phase research experience in a broad range of indications and client types Required
7-9 years in a pharmaceutical and/or CRO setting, serving in a global Clinical Trial Team Lead or Global Project Management role or equivalent Required
4-6 years supervisory experience in a similar work environment. Required
Demonstrable track record of success delivering complex and high priority clinical trials within agreed time, quality and cost working across multiple therapeutic areas, phases 1 to 4, in a global capacity. High
Demonstrated experience in developing and fostering strong client and internal relationships. High
Thorough understanding of ICH GCP and applicable global regulatory regulations and guidelines. High
Skilled in MS Office Suite of products and strong working knowledge of Clinical Trial Management Systems, electronic Trial Master File, and electronic Data Capture systems and solutions. High
Successful record in managing diverse staff and leading strong teams. Experience in both direct and indirect supervision responsibilities. High
Additional project management certifications such as PMP and training are an asset High
Excellent verbal and written communication skills. High

If you’re looking for a career where your work advances global health
and where scientific excellence meets real-world impact
, join us and be part of something bigger. One Team, One Purpose.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Syphilis Free Start
new_jobs.description:
About Evidence Action

At Evidence Action, we deliver data-driven interventions that transform lives at an unprecedented scale. We identify neglected global health issues and deploy proven solutions, forging healthier futures for generations.

Our model operationalizes leading academic research (including from Nobel-winning economists). We measure progress and outcomes at every stage to ensure we're making a real impact for people living in poverty and suffering from preventable or treatable health issues. Operating across 11 countries, our team of 900+ has reached over 500 million people, working closely with governments to scale these interventions.

Our Deworm the World program has delivered over 2 billion treatments, significantly reducing worm prevalence and generating more than $23 billion in lifetime productivity gains.
Through Safe Water Now, we've saved the lives of over 15,000 children.
Our Accelerator explores untapped opportunities in global health, testing low-cost interventions with the greatest potential to save and improve lives.

At Evidence Action, your colleagues are your greatest asset. You'll partner with high-caliber colleagues in an environment blending innovation, autonomy, and teamwork. Our team excels in disruptive thinking and believes in rolling up our sleeves to get things done. If you're looking to work flexibly and with purpose, join a team that delivers measurable change for millions.

About the SFS Program and Role:

Every year, there are over 200,000 stillbirths and newborn deaths and over 100,000 instances of disability among newborns because of a preventable infection; maternal syphilis. In fact, the infection causes more stillbirths and newborn deaths than pediatric HIV, yet receives only a fraction of the resources.

Through our Syphilis-Free Start (SFS) program, our aim is to close syphilis screening gaps via introduction of HIV/syphilis dual testing and to close treatment gaps by implementing strategies to address context-specific treatment barriers for women who test positive for syphilis. We've already reached mothers across Liberia, Zambia, Cameroon, and Côte d'Ivoire, with new pilots underway in Indonesia and are continuing to scope our programs in additional geographies.

Reporting to our Associate Director, you will lead Evidence Action's work to test what else the SFS model can do. You will shape the design and rigorous assessment of new theories of change for the program, looking at what new health outcomes the model could credibly deliver, new platforms through which maternal syphilis testing and treatment could be delivered, and new geographies and health system contexts where our model might fit. The role combines program design leadership with strong monitoring, evaluation, and data analysis skills, and is accountable for producing clear, evidence-based recommendations on whether and how each new direction should be pursued at scale.

Key Responsibilities:

Theory of Change and Program Model Design

Design testable program models to answer the program's open questions on outcomes, delivery platform, and technology, specifying what would justify scale-up
Develop and pressure-test the theory of change for expanding the program's outcome set beyond syphilis, including the pathway to HIV and hepatitis B impact and the assumptions each pathway depends on
Assess alternative service delivery platforms such as private and faith-based facilities, community-based outreach, and other entry points
Work with the global MLE team and the Data & Learning Manager to define formative research questions, measurement frameworks, and evaluation approaches for each pilot

Pilot Execution & Program Management

Oversee day-to-day pilot implementation, including partner and contract management, rollout, training, and troubleshooting
Adapt management approaches to different delivery models, including pilots run by local implementing partners or contracted firms
Contribute to program planning, workplans, and reporting, and flag issues, timeline risks, or scope changes early to the Associate Director, SFS
Provide program input into baseline and endline design, and support integration of indicators into HMIS and DHIS2 where feasible

Emerging Technology Assessment

Track the antenatal diagnostic landscape and maintain an informed view on which emerging products, including triplex HIV/syphilis/hepatitis B tests and treponemal/non-treponemal test combinations, to determine which merit assessment for program introduction
Assess candidate technologies against the operational realities of program contexts: cost and procurement pathways, regulatory and national guideline requirements, provider workflow and training burden, testing algorithm complexity, and the referral and treatment pathways each result triggers
Design and lead introduction pilots for selected technologies, in partnership with the global MLE team and Ministry counterparts, and produce clear recommendations on whether and how to proceed, provided funding for such activities is secured

Analysis, Recommendations, and Learning

Synthesize pilot findings into clear, decision-oriented assessments of feasibility, effectiveness, and scale-up potential, with an explicit recommendation on each theory of change tested
Support quantitative and qualitative data analysis, in collaboration with the MLE team, using tools such as Stata, R, or Excel
Develop concrete recommendations for program adaptation, including changes to policy, service delivery, testing algorithms, and implementation models
Share learnings across pilot geographies and the SFS portfolio, and translate them for external technical audiences

Country Engagement

Serve as Evidence Action's primary point of contact with Ministries of Health and other stakeholders in pilot geographies
Oversee and manage local implementing partners and contractors to support pilot implementation in-country
Share findings and recommendations with Ministries so that scale-up decisions reflect government priorities

Requirements

A Masters in public health, epidemiology, statistics, public policy, or a related field
Minimum 5-7 years of experience in global health programs, with both program management experience and a monitoring, learning, and evaluation (MLE) background in LMIC contexts
You have designed program models for new interventions or pilots, and defined how to measure them (indicators, data collection, and evaluation approach), not only monitored or evaluated models designed by others.
You have used evidence to make recommendations to continue, adapt, or stop a program
You have experience managing routine data collection and analysis
Strong quantitative skills and data analysis (proficiency in Stata, R, or equivalent preferred)
You have operated as both a program lead and an MLE lead with the ability to shape a program model and rigorously test it
You are able to adapt your communications style for teams at different skill levels and across different cultural contexts internally and externally. and experience producing clear, decision-oriented reports for program and donor audiences
You have the ability to manage complex and interdependent projects and build structured, but flexible, processes
You enjoy building processes from ambiguity and can help the team operate across low resource program contexts and adapt approaches to available infrastructure and systems
French language skills, both spoken and written, is preferred but not required

Location

This role will be based remotely within the United States. You are welcome but not required to work out of Evidence Action's office in Washington, DC. Evidence Action team members work across timezones in the US, Africa, and Asia, and meetings may be scheduled to best capture team needs. This role requires regular international travel (:30%) to Indonesia, Madagascar, and other new geographies, particularly during pilot start-up and data collection periods.

Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration
, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems
across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide
, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.

Fully remote and global,
we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform
. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified.
Visionary
in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™
for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026
Most Flexible Companies
, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

About The Role

Camunda partners with global system integrators, regional consultancies, and technology partners to help enterprises orchestrate complex processes and AI agents. This role builds and runs the engine behind that partner business: the program, the investments, the data, and the operating rhythm. The Principal Program Manager is the strategic operating partner to the VP of Partnerships & Alliances and leads an AI-first approach to how the partner team works.

Partner program, fund, and data work currently sits with the VP and the partner managers, which limits scale and pulls partner managers away from selling with partners. Partner-sourced and influenced pipeline, MDF spend, and the Strategic GSI Co-Investment Program all need consistent governance and reporting that no one owns today.

What You Will Do

Partner with the VP to run the organization: own the annual partner plan, budget and headcount planning, the team's operating rhythm, and executive and board reporting.
Drive team performance and accountability through clear OKRs, scorecards, and pipeline reviews.
Own the global partner program: partner types, tiers, reseller and commercial models, onboarding, benefits, agreements, and the annual program refresh.
Manage MDF and co-op budgets end to end: planning, approvals, claims, proof of performance, and ROI reporting.
Run the program office for the Strategic GSI Co-Investment Program: funded head scorecards, quarterly KPI gates, investment release decisions, and executive steering.
Manage priority partners through program parameters, and give Regional and GSI Partner Managers the standards, data, and tools they need.
Run the Partner Advisory Board and the annual partner calendar, including webinars, newsletters, and program communications.
Serve as the partner team's liaison to Marketing and Marketing Ops, Legal, Finance, Sales Ops, Enablement, and Product.
Own partner operations and tools, including Impartner (PRM) and Salesforce: deal registration, attribution, data quality, and dashboards. Support hyperscaler marketplace and co-sell operations.
Design and ship AI agents and automations across the partner lifecycle, and measure the time and cost they save.

What You Will Bring

8+ years in partner, channel, or alliances roles at enterprise software or SaaS companies, with 3+ years running partner programs or partner operations.
Direct experience managing MDF and GSI co-investments or funded head programs, including ROI tracking and stage-gated funding.
Deep knowledge of partner types, tiering, and reseller and route-to-market models.
Hands-on experience as a builder (not just a user) of a PRM platform, ideally Impartner, and Salesforce.
Proven use of AI tools, agents, and automation to redesign workflows, with examples you can show.
Experience running a partner advisory board or a similar executive partner forum.
Strong analytical skills: builds own reports and can explain the numbers to executives and Finance.
Strategic judgment and executive presence, with experience as a trusted strategic operator to a senior leader.
Clear written communication and the ability to run programs across regions and time zones.

Nice to Have

Experience with hyperscaler marketplaces and co-sell programs.
Background in process orchestration, automation, or integration software.
Experience at a high-growth company scaling from early partner motion to a global program.

This role is an existing vacancy

What We Have to Offer:

We offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. Salary ranges are location-based, with Standard and Major markets (global tech hubs) reflecting local competition.

(base salary + 100% variable target, where applicable) shown below spans from the minimum in a Standard market to the maximum in a Major market. Final offers depend on skills
, experience

(our global employer partner), and your Talent Acquisition Partner will provide a personalized Total Rewards Calculator
after your first interview.

.

Benefits & Perks

We invest in your wellbeing, growth, and ability to connect, along with perks that support you no matter where you’re based. Our benefits are globally designed and locally delivered where applicable.

Remote & Flexible: Work from anywhere with the setup that suits you, home office budget, co-working space support, and flexible time off to recharge when you need it.
In Person Connection: We invest in meaningful face time through our Annual Kickoff (Vienna in 2025, Madrid in 2026!), team offsites, and Camundi Connection Budgets, including contributing to meetups while travelling,, and local gatherings with fellow Camundi.
Health & Wellbeing: Access locally tailored healthcare, Modern Health for global mental wellbeing, and our Live Well Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA), a flexible, global benefit that puts you in control of your whole life, not just work, from: staying active, to caring for family, exploring personal passions, meaningful experiences, and investing in your financial wellbeing. The Live Well program launches in 2026 and scales to €1,000 annually from 2027.

new_jobs.title: Health & Safety Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Securitas USA

Securitas Security Services USA, Inc. is a global leader in protective services, delivering specialized guarding, advanced technology, and risk management across many industries. Our mission is to help make your world a safer place. For 90 years, we’ve built our business on trust, innovation, and international expertise, providing tailored security solutions that combine cutting-edge technology with exceptional service.

Location:
Remote (must reside in the US)

Travel:
Up to 25%

Salary Range:
$110,000–$120,000 annually, depending on location, experience, and skills

What You’ll Do

As a Health & Safety Program Manager, you will drive Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) performance in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. You’ll design and manage safety programs tailored to client needs and own both operational performance and risk management outcomes.

You will support the Datacenter Physical Security & Safety program by providing expert EHS guidance, incident management, and program coordination across the region.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Program Management

Support EHS activities in the region, aligning with client expectations and Securitas standards.
Ensure compliance with OSHA and other applicable regulations.
Build strong client relationships and provide structure and direction for the EHS team.
Identify and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency.
Perform other duties as needed to support the Datacenter Physical Security & Safety program.

Incident & Risk Management

Lead remote incident management for injuries, from intake through root cause analysis and corrective actions.
Handle EHS escalations, including occasional weekends and holidays.
Provide timely, accurate communication to stakeholders during escalations.
Conduct annual reviews of safety-related documents with stakeholders.

Client Relations & Communication

Develop and deliver presentations in partnership with field operations and subject matter experts.
Present EHS performance, risks, and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
Maintain a customer service mindset and partner with the client to resolve issues.
Schedule and facilitate client and internal meetings using client meeting tools.

Operational Excellence & Data Management

Coordinate EHS-related projects with training, communications, and project management teams.
Manage EHS databases and reporting; use Power BI and Excel to build and analyze reports and dashboards.
Ensure proper EHS document retention per client and company requirements.

Who You Are

You bring:

A service-first mindset, clear communication, and strong attention to detail.
A solutions-focused approach and the ability to work both independently and in teams.
Comfort in a fast-paced environment with frequent stakeholder interaction and occasional off-hours escalations.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Science, or a related field; or equivalent experience.

Certifications

Professional safety certifications (CSP, ASP, CHST, or similar) preferred.

Skills And Experience

Must-Have

At least three years of program management experience with Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) programs and OSHA or similar regulatory frameworks.
Experience with Data Center Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) programs.
Strong Power BI and Excel skills for data analysis, reporting, and dashboard creation.
Proven ability to develop and deliver presentations to senior stakeholders.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including incident and escalation reporting.
Experience managing multiple projects and priorities in a dynamic environment.
Strong relationship-building skills with clients, field operations, and cross-functional teams.

Nice-to-Have

Experience in EHS program management within datacenter, technology, or critical infrastructure environments.
Knowledge of datacenter operations, physical security, or related industries.
Experience with remote incident management and multi-site EHS support.
Professional safety certifications (CSP, ASP, CHST, or similar).

Why you would want to join the team

Direct impact on the safety and well-being of employees and contractors in a critical datacenter environment.
Regular interaction with high-level client stakeholders and Securitas leadership.
Opportunities to grow within Securitas’ broader Health & Safety and operational leadership structure.
Supportive leadership and a collaborative team focused on continuous improvement and learning.
Exposure to advanced technology environments and complex EHS challenges.
A strong partnership with the client and a culture that values proactive safety and clear communication.

Make an Impact at Securitas USA

Securitas USA employees come from all walks of life, bringing a variety of skills, experiences, and perspectives. United by a shared purpose, we help make the world a safer place. We provide security services to meet the unique needs of our clients to help safeguard their people and assets.

At Securitas USA, our core values are the foundation of everything we do. Represented by the three red dots in our logo, Integrity, Vigilance, and Helpfulness
guide how we serve our clients, support our colleagues, and engage with our communities.

Integrity

We act with honesty, accountability, and professionalism in everything we do, and we foster a culture where transparency, respect, and ethical behavior are expected.

Vigilance

We stay alert, aware, and attentive to our surroundings. Through observing and reporting, our employees help identify potential risks and respond to situations that may impact safety and security.

Helpfulness

We are approachable and service-oriented, whether assisting a client, colleague, or member of the community.

Securitas USA is committed to equal employment opportunity. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, pregnancy, genetic information, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other applicable legally protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodation: Securitas USA is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. In keeping with our commitment, Securitas USA will take steps to assure the people with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations. Accordingly, if reasonable accommodation is required to fully participate in the job application or interview process, to perform the essential functions of the position, and/or to receive all other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact PrivacyRequests@securitasinc.com.
